title: Book One · Chapter 165: Another Pair of Hands
story:
Two children have made a drawing of the food shop. They are in Ronan's class. Ronan thought it would be smaller. He looks at its two wide sides. He looks at the empty place on the plan. He tries to fit the paper shape there.

One corner covers Mei's window picture. Another reaches the doorway. He lifts the shape and tries the other wall.

“It can go on its own board,” Mei says.

“We do not have another board.”

The girl points to the classroom shelf. She helped make the drawing. Another class used a plain board for their project. It is on the shelf now. She already asked Miss Wu, “May we use that board?” The teacher said yes, if they put it back afterwards.

Ronan looks at her. He thought they needed to find another board. But the girl has already found a board. Miss Wu said they could use it.

“Who said we can show the shop?” he asks.

The woman works in that shop. She gave the children a short note. They show him the drawing she saw. The woman checked the words underneath it too. There is nothing about her family or her money. She makes food each morning. The card lists her food.

Ronan puts the note with the permission papers. He does not change the words to sound like his own cards. The two children made this picture. The shopkeeper has checked their words. Ronan can help find a safe place for the board.

Miss Wu tries it on the long table. It can stand against the wall, away from the edge. An adult will fix it in place during setup. It will not need another chair or more floor space.

The boy helped draw the food pictures. He can stay and explain them for a short time. He must leave early with his family. “What time must you leave?” Ronan asks. He writes the boy's answer down. Then the boy checks the time on the paper.

“Can I still play the game?” the boy asks.

Leo holds up the joke door. “Only if you find your way out again.”

Everyone laughs. The boy reads one clue. He tries it and gets the right answer. Then he asks Ronan, “Where will your picture be?”

Ronan looks at the cat drawing. It is the smallest one now. He has given much of the room to other people's work. For a moment he wants to move the cat into the middle.

He puts it near the street map instead. It shows the cat he often sees in the yard. Visitors can look at it beside the map. The pot hides the feet he could not draw well.

At home Mum asks, “Is the room ready?” Ronan tells her about the food-shop picture. More things are ready now. He is not making every part himself.

“Does that make it easier?”

“Some parts. There are more people to ask.”

“And more people to answer.”

He thinks of the borrowed board and the checked food card. That is true too.

He takes out the carrying list. There is no new heavy thing under Mum's name. The two children will bring the food picture on Friday. Their adults will come to help them carry it. Ronan adds them to the plan, then puts the pencil down. There will be another good picture in the room. The two children have their own adults to help. Their families will help carry it too.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：made＝做了、制作了；shopkeeper＝店主、看店的人；in place＝在适当位置。

情节提示：permission＝同意、许可；setup＝布置；borrowed＝借来的。

理解：1. 新加入的画为什么不需要由 Ronan 全部重做？2. 他最后把自己的猫画安排在哪里？
